GUI.note:
Assessment
42-year-old female never-smoker presenting for evaluation of incidental bilateral lower lobe thin-walled lung cysts (3-10 mm, with normal intervening lung parenchyma) and a 2.4 cm left renal angiomyolipoma identified on abdominal CT (2024-05-10). History is notable for a prior spontaneous left pneumothorax in 2021 treated with chest tube drainage, and 1 year of mild exertional dyspnea. She has no stigmata or family history of tuberous sclerosis complex (no skin lesions, seizures, or intellectual disability).

Differential Diagnosis for Diffuse Cystic Lung Disease:
1. Sporadic Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (S-LAM) - Most likely diagnosis. The triad of reproductive-age female, numerous round thin-walled pulmonary cysts with normal intervening parenchyma, history of spontaneous pneumothorax, and renal angiomyolipoma is classic for LAM. Per ATS/JRS guidelines, a definitive diagnosis of LAM can be established noninvasively (without lung biopsy) based on characteristic HRCT chest findings in the presence of a renal angiomyolipoma and/or elevated serum VEGF-D (>=800 pg/mL).
